Prealgebra · Lesson 5.4

Rounding and Estimation

Solve this lesson →All lessons

A step counter reads 4,7324,732, and you round it to 4,7004,700. The halfway mark between 4,7004,700 and 4,8004,800 is 4,7504,750, and 4,7324,732 falls below it, so you round down. That single comparison is all rounding is. This lesson turns it into a one-digit check and then handles ties, carries, and negative values.

Problem
Round 4,7324,732 to the nearest hundred. The midpoint between 4,7004,700 and 4,8004,800 is 4,7504,750. Which neighbor is 4,7324,732 closer to?
Show a hint
  • Mark the two neighbors 4,7004,700 and 4,8004,800 and find the point exactly between them. Then ask which side of that point 4,7324,732 falls on.
  • The midpoint is 4,7504,750. Since 4,7324,732 is below 4,7504,750, it is closer to the neighbor on the left, which is 4,7004,700.
Show the full solution
4,7324,732 sits between 4,7004,700 and 4,8004,800, and the midpoint is 4,7504,750. Since 4,7324,732 is below that, it leans toward the lower neighbor. The gap down is 3232 and the gap up is 6868, so the nearest hundred is 47004700​. Only a value at or above 4,7504,750 would tick up to 4,8004,800.
Problem
A festival shows 68,43168,431 attendees. Round to the nearest thousand. The deciding digit is the hundreds digit. What is 68,43168,431 rounded to the nearest thousand?
Show a hint
  • The place you are rounding to is the thousands place, the 88 in 68,43168,431. The digit that decides what happens to it is the next one to the right, the hundreds digit. Circle that digit and ask whether it is big enough to push the thousands place up.
  • The hundreds digit is 44. Since 44 is 44 or less, the thousands digit stays as it is, it does not tick up. Now drop everything to the right of the thousands place to zero and read off the result.
Show the full solution
The thousands digit is the 88, so the answer is either 68,00068,000 or 69,00069,000. The deciding digit is the one just to its right, the hundreds digit 44. Since 44 is under 55, the thousands digit stays put and everything after it drops to zero. 68,431≈68,00068,431≈68,000​ The midpoint check agrees, since 68,43168,431 is below 68,50068,500.
Problem
Round 2,9502,950 to the nearest hundred. The value lands exactly on the midpoint 2,9502,950, so the tie rule sends it up. The hundreds digit is 99, so a carry rolls forward. What is the result?
Show a hint
  • Find the two nearest hundreds that hug 2,9502,950, then find the midpoint between them. Which way does the tie rule send you?
  • You are rounding up from 2,9002,900 toward 3,0003,000. The hundreds digit is a 9 and cannot go to 10, so the carry pushes into the thousands. The result is the next clean hundred above 2,9502,950.
Show the full solution
The hundreds on either side of 2,9502,950 are 2,9002,900 and 3,0003,000, and the midpoint is 2,9502,950 itself. A tie rounds to the larger value, so we go up to 30003000​. The hundreds digit is a 99, so it cannot climb. It rolls to 00 and carries 11 into the thousands, turning the 22 into a 33.
Problem
A 3D printer reads 7.837.83 m of filament remaining. Round to the nearest tenth. The hundredths digit 33 decides. What is 7.837.83 rounded to the nearest tenth?
Show a hint
  • Your two neighbors are 7.87.8 and 7.97.9, and the line between them is at 7.857.85. The only digit that decides which neighbor you get is the hundredths digit, the one right after the tenths place.
  • The hundredths digit of 7.837.83 is 33. Since 7.837.83 is below the midpoint 7.857.85, it stays with the lower neighbor. Keep the tenths digit as it is and drop the rest.
Show the full solution
The tenths on either side of 7.837.83 are 7.87.8 and 7.97.9, and the midpoint is 7.857.85. The hundredths digit is 33, so the reading sits below the midpoint and stays with the lower neighbor. Keep the tenths digit and drop the rest, giving 7.87.8​.
Problem
A tide gauge reads 3.6173.617 m. The harbor chart records to the nearest hundredth. The thousandths digit 77 decides. Round 3.6173.617 to the nearest hundredth.
Show a hint
  • You only care about which side of the midpoint 3.6153.615 the reading falls on. Compare 3.6173.617 to 3.6153.615. Is it below the midpoint, at the midpoint, or above it?
  • The digit that decides everything is the one just past the hundredths place, the thousandths digit. Here that digit is 77. Anything 55 or higher tips you up to the larger neighbor, so keep two digits after the point and bump the hundredths up.
Show the full solution
The hundredths on either side of 3.6173.617 are 3.613.61 and 3.623.62, and the midpoint is 3.6153.615. The thousandths digit is 77, which is 55 or more, so round up. The harbor chart records 3.623.62​. The distances agree, since 3.6173.617 is 0.0070.007 above 3.613.61 but only 0.0030.003 below 3.623.62.
Problem
A lab scale reads 1.9951.995 grams. Round to the nearest hundredth. The thousandths digit 55 is a tie, so round up. The hundredths digit is 99, triggering a carry. What is the result?
Show a hint
  • The deciding digit is the thousandths digit, the 55 in 1.995‾1.995​. A 55 is the exact halfway case, so round the hundredths place up to the larger value. The only catch is that the digit you are bumping is a 99, so think about where it goes when it cannot just become a 1010.
  • Bumping the hundredths 99 up writes a 00 there and carries 11 into the tenths place. But the tenths digit is also 99, so it becomes 00 and carries 11 into the ones place, turning 11 into 22. So 1.991.99 climbs to 2.002.00. Keep both decimal places.
Show the full solution
Keeping two decimal places makes the thousandths digit the decider, and here it is 55 with nothing behind it, an exact tie. So the hundredths place rounds up. That digit is a 99, so it becomes 00 and carries 11 into the tenths, which is also 99, so that becomes 00 and carries into the ones, lifting the 11 to a 22. 1.995≈2.001.995≈2.00​ Keep both zeros, since the notebook still records two decimal places.
Key idea
The rounding rule. To round to a place, look at the digit just after it, called the deciding digit. If it is 55 or more, the rounding place goes up by one. If it is 44 or less, that place stays the same. Either way, every digit after the rounding place becomes zero. You never have to measure the distance to the midpoint, because that one digit tells you which half you are in. If the deciding digit is 55 and only zeros follow it, the number sits on the midpoint. That is a tie, and this course rounds every tie to the larger value. There is one special case. If the rounding place holds a 99, going up makes it 00 and carries 11 into the place on its left, as in addition. If that carry passes the leading digit, the number gains a digit, which is how 9.969.96 rounds to 10.010.0.
Problem
A freezer reads −83−83 degrees. Round to the nearest ten. The neighbors are −90−90 and −80−80. Measure each gap and pick the closer one. What is the result?
Show a hint
  • Find the gap from −83−83 to each neighbor. How far is it left to −90−90, and how far right to −80−80? The shorter trip wins.
  • From −83−83 it is 77 steps left to reach −90−90, but only 33 steps right to reach −80−80. The nearer multiple of ten is −80−80.
Show the full solution
The multiples of ten around −83−83 are −90−90 and −80−80. The gap down to −90−90 is 77, and the gap up to −80−80 is only 33, so the technician records −80−80​ degrees. Negatives use the same midpoint test as positives. The midpoint here is −85−85, and −83−83 sits to the right of it.
Problem
A thermostat reads −2.35−2.35 degrees. Round to the nearest tenth. −2.35−2.35 is the exact midpoint between −2.4−2.4 and −2.3−2.3. The tie rule rounds to the larger value. What does the display show?
Show a hint
  • Forget the minus sign for a second and just picture the number line. Mark −2.4−2.4 on the left and −2.3−2.3 on the right, then drop −2.35−2.35 in between. Is it closer to one of them, or stuck dead in the middle?
  • It is a perfect tie, so use the rule, round to the larger value. "Larger" means farther to the right on the number line. Between −2.4−2.4 and −2.3−2.3, the one on the right is −2.3−2.3, so that is your answer.
Show the full solution
The tenths around −2.35−2.35 are −2.4−2.4 and −2.3−2.3, and −2.35−2.35 is 0.050.05 from each, so it is an exact tie. A tie rounds to the larger value, and the larger of two negatives is the one farther right. The display shows −2.3−2.3​. It feels backwards because 2.32.3 is less than 2.42.4, but with the minus signs attached, −2.3−2.3 is the bigger number.
Key idea
Rounding negatives. A negative number rounds to the nearer multiple exactly like a positive one. The only thing to watch is what larger means for negatives. Larger means farther to the right on the number line, so between two negatives the larger one is the one closer to zero. When a negative value lands exactly on a midpoint, the round-to-the-larger tie rule rounds toward zero, which is why −2.35−2.35 rounds to −2.3−2.3 and not −2.4−2.4.
Problem
Three crates weigh 487487, 213213, and 356356 kg. Round each to the nearest hundred, then add the rounded values. What is your estimated total?
Show a hint
  • Handle one crate at a time. Look at the part of each weight after the hundreds and decide whether it pushes the number up to the next hundred or leaves it at the hundred below.
  • Round each one. 487487 is past the halfway mark so it becomes 500500, 213213 is below halfway so it becomes 200200, and 356356 is past halfway so it becomes 400400. Now add 500+200+400500+200+400.
Show the full solution
For 487487, the leftover past the hundred is 8787, above 5050, so it rounds up to 500500. For 213213 the leftover is 1313, so it stays at 200200. For 356356 the leftover is 5656, so it rounds up to 400400. Adding gives 500+200+400=1100500+200+400=1100​. The exact total is 1,0561,056, so the estimate tells you instantly whether the van is near its limit.
Problem
A field-trip invoice lists 2929 students at 6.106.10 dollars each, printing 1,7691,769 dollars. Round each to a friendly value and multiply. What is your quick estimate of 29×6.1029×6.10?
Show a hint
  • You are not finding the exact total here, you are building a quick comparison number. Replace each part with a friendly nearby value first. What is 2929 rounded to the nearest ten, and what is 6.106.10 rounded to the nearest whole dollar?
  • Rounding 2929 to the nearest ten gives 3030, since 2929 is much closer to 3030 than to 2020. Rounding 6.106.10 to the nearest whole dollar gives 66, since 6.106.10 is just past 66. Now multiply 30×630×6.
Show the full solution
2929 rounds to 3030 at the nearest ten, and 6.106.10 rounds to 66 at the nearest dollar, since 1010 cents is nowhere near the 6.506.50 midpoint. Multiplying the friendly numbers gives 30×6=18030×6=180​. The printed 1,7691,769 is about ten times that, the signature of a decimal point that slipped one spot. The exact total is 176.90176.90.
Key idea
Estimation as an error check. To estimate, round each number to an easy value and then combine the rounded values. The result is not exact, so write it with ≈≈, like 29×6.10≈18029×6.10≈180, never with an equals sign. An estimate is close enough to catch a large error. When a printed total like 1,7691,769 is ten times your estimate of about 180180, you know something is wrong before doing any careful work.
Fun fact
In 1856 surveyors measured Everest and got exactly 29,00029,000 feet. Worried a round number would look like a guess, they published 29,00229,002 feet, inventing two feet to appear more precise.
Problem
A gauge is rounded to the nearest tenth and reports 4.34.3 mm. The original reading was stored to two decimal places. What is the largest two-decimal value that still rounds to 4.34.3?
Show a hint
  • The reported 4.34.3 covers everything from 4.254.25 up to but not including 4.354.35. You only need the values in that stretch that have exactly two decimal places, so start at the top end and step downward.
  • Check 4.354.35 first. It sits exactly halfway between 4.34.3 and 4.44.4, so by the larger-value rule it rounds up to 4.44.4, not 4.34.3. That means 4.354.35 is out. Step down one hundredth to 4.344.34 and round it to the nearest tenth to see where it lands.
Show the full solution
A reported 4.34.3 covers everything from 4.254.25 up to just under 4.354.35, because 4.354.35 is a tie that rounds up to 4.44.4 instead. The largest two-decimal value in that stretch is 4.344.34​, whose hundredths digit 44 sends it down to 4.34.3. The band is half-open, so the lower end is included and the upper end is not.
Key idea
Rounding is one-way. Rounding replaces an exact number with a nearby easier one, and the exact number cannot be recovered afterward. A rounded 4.34.3 does not stand for a single value. It stands for an interval, from the lower midpoint 4.254.25 up to just under the upper midpoint 4.354.35, because every number in that interval rounds to 4.34.3. Many different numbers round to the same value, so all you can recover are the two boundaries the original lies between.
Problem
A price rounds to 77 at the nearest dollar, to 6.86.8 at the nearest tenth, and its hundredths digit is 00. Exactly one price to the cent satisfies all three. What is it?
Show a hint
  • Turn each clue into an interval. Rounding to the nearest whole dollar gives 77, so the price runs from 6.56.5 up to just under 7.57.5. Rounding to the nearest tenth gives 6.86.8, so the price runs from 6.756.75 up to just under 6.856.85. The price must sit inside both ranges at once, which means inside the tighter one.
  • The overlap of the two ranges is 6.756.75 up to just under 6.856.85. Now list the prices in that band whose hundredths digit is 00. The candidates ending in zero cents are 6.806.80. Check the only one that lands in the band.
Show the full solution
Rounding to 77 at the nearest dollar means 6.5≤p<7.56.5≤p<7.5. Rounding to 6.86.8 at the nearest tenth means 6.75≤p<6.856.75≤p<6.85, which sits entirely inside the first range. The prices to the cent in that band run 6.756.75 through 6.846.84, and the only one with a hundredths digit of 00 is 6.806.80​. Turning each rounding clue into a range and overlapping them is the standard way to pin a value down.

Practice these ideas

Practice
A scoreboard reads 7,2847,284 fans. The press box reports to the nearest hundred. What is 7,2847,284 rounded to the nearest hundred?
Show the solution
The hundreds around 7,2847,284 are 7,2007,200 and 7,3007,300, and the midpoint is 7,2507,250. Since 7,2847,284 is above the midpoint, it climbs, and the press box reports 73007300​ fans.
Practice
A fundraiser total of 3,5003,500 dollars is to be printed rounded to the nearest thousand. 3,5003,500 is the exact midpoint. Using the half-way-up rule, what goes on the banner?
Show the solution
3,5003,500 is 500500 from 3,0003,000 and 500500 from 4,0004,000, so neither thousand is closer. That is an exact tie, and our rule sends a tie to the larger value, so the banner reads 40004000​.
Practice
A scale reads 6.476.47 kg. A recipe records to the nearest tenth. Round 6.476.47 to the nearest tenth.
Show the solution
The tenths around 6.476.47 are 6.46.4 and 6.56.5, and the midpoint is 6.456.45. The hundredths digit is 77, which is 55 or more, so the tenths digit goes up by one and 6.476.47 rounds to 6.56.5​.
Practice
A lap is timed at 0.3820.382 seconds. The results sheet keeps two decimal places. Round 0.3820.382 to the nearest hundredth.
Show the solution
The hundredths around 0.3820.382 are 0.380.38 and 0.390.39, and the midpoint is 0.3850.385. The thousandths digit is 22, below 55, so the hundredths digit stays and everything after it is dropped, giving 0.380.38​. The gaps confirm it, 0.0020.002 down versus 0.0080.008 up.
Practice
A bus ride takes exactly 9.59.5 minutes. The schedule lists whole minutes only. 9.59.5 is exactly halfway between 99 and 1010. What whole number does the schedule show?
Show the solution
9.59.5 is 0.50.5 from 99 and 0.50.5 from 1010, so it is an exact tie. A tie rounds to the larger value, so the schedule lists the trip as 1010​ minutes.
Practice
A fitness band reads 0.650.65 battery and rounds to one decimal place. 0.650.65 is exactly halfway between 0.60.6 and 0.70.7. What does the band display?
Show the solution
0.650.65 is 0.050.05 from 0.60.6 and 0.050.05 from 0.70.7, so it is a perfect tie. A tie rounds to the larger value, so the fitness band shows 0.70.7​.
Practice
A caliper reads 0.3960.396 cm and the spec sheet keeps two decimal places. The thousandths digit 66 rounds the hundredths 99 up, triggering a carry. Round 0.3960.396 to the nearest hundredth.
Show the solution
The hundredths digit of 0.3960.396 is the 99, and the thousandths digit 66 is at least 55, so that 99 rounds up. A 99 cannot become a single-digit 1010, so it turns into 00 and carries 11 into the tenths, taking 33 to 44. That gives 0.400.40​. Keep the trailing zero so the answer still shows the hundredths place the spec sheet asked for.
Practice
A fuel gauge reads 8.978.97 liters and the trip computer shows one decimal place. The tenths digit is 99, so rounding it up triggers a carry into the ones. Round 8.978.97 to the nearest tenth.
Show the solution
The hundredths digit of 8.978.97 is 77, which is at least 55, so the tenths place rounds up. The tenths digit is already 99, so it rolls over to 00 and carries 11 into the ones, taking the 88 to 99. The trip computer shows 9.09.0​. Write the trailing zero to show the value was rounded to the nearest tenth.
Practice
A wind-chill of −46−46 degrees is reported to the nearest ten. The two neighboring tens are −50−50 and −40−40, with midpoint −45−45. Which side is −46−46 on? Round −46−46 to the nearest ten.
Show the solution
The multiples of ten around −46−46 are −50−50 and −40−40. The gap to −50−50 is 44 and the gap to −40−40 is 66, so −46−46 rounds to −50−50​. The midpoint is −45−45, and −46−46 sits to the left of it, so there is no tie to break.
Practice
An elevation app shows −3.5−3.5 m. The value is exactly halfway between −4−4 and −3−3. The larger of those two is closer to zero. Round −3.5−3.5 to the nearest whole number.
Show the solution
−3.5−3.5 is exactly halfway between −4−4 and −3−3, so closeness cannot decide and the half-way rule takes over. Larger means farther right on the number line, and −3−3 is right of −4−4, so the elevation rounds to −3−3​ meters. Between two negatives, the larger one is always the one closer to zero.
Practice
A freezer probe reads −1.25−1.25 degrees. The app rounds to the nearest tenth. −1.25−1.25 is an exact tie between −1.3−1.3 and −1.2−1.2. Round to the larger value. What does the app display?
Show the solution
−1.25−1.25 is 0.050.05 from −1.3−1.3 and 0.050.05 from −1.2−1.2, so it is an exact tie. A tie goes to the larger value, and −1.2−1.2 lies to the right of −1.3−1.3 on the number line, so the app displays −1.2−1.2​.
Practice
A concert order lists 4141 tickets at 19.8019.80 dollars each, printing a total of 81.1881.18 dollars. Round each to the nearest friendly value and multiply. What is your quick estimate?
Show the solution
4141 has a ones digit of 11, so it rounds down to 4040. 19.8019.80 has 8080 cents, past the 5050 mark, so it rounds up to 2020 dollars. Multiplying gives 40×20=80040×20=800​. The printed 81.1881.18 is nowhere near that ballpark, so the receipt is almost certainly missing a digit.
Practice
Three boxes weigh 596596, 207207, and 398398 grams. Round each to the nearest hundred, then add. What is the estimated total?
Show the solution
Round each weight to the nearest hundred one at a time. For 596596, the tens digit is 99, which is well past halfway, so it rounds up to 600600. For 207207, the tens digit is 00, so it rounds down to 200200. For 398398, the tens digit is 99, so it rounds up to 400400. Now add the friendly numbers, 600+200+400=1200600+200+400=1200. The estimate clears the 10001000 gram mark with room to spare. 12001200​
Practice
A rain gauge stores readings to the nearest hundredth but its display shows the nearest tenth, reading 5.35.3 mm. What is the smallest two-decimal stored value that rounds to 5.35.3?
Show the solution
The tenths around the stored reading are 5.25.2 and 5.35.3, and the midpoint is 5.255.25. By the half-way rule that midpoint rounds up to 5.35.3, while 5.245.24 would drop to 5.25.2. The smallest qualifying value is 5.255.25​.
